p:cNvPr.descr: A complex diagram showing how oligosaccharides are synthesized inside the lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum. At the top right side of the diagram, there is a box containing the structure of dolichol phosphate (n = 9-22). The bulk of the structure is an 11-carbon chain. The left end of the chain has a phosphate group bonded to it, represented by a circled P. The third carbon over is bonded up to CH3. There is a 4-carbon region of the chain, in the middle, with one flattened double bond, the right carbon of which bonds down to CH3. This region is in parentheses with n on the right, indicating that this part of the chain can repeat 9-22 times. To the right of this are three more carbons, with one flattened double bond. The carbon on the far right end bonds up and right and down and right to CH3. At the upper left corner of the diagram is a key containing the colored shapes which represent oligosaccharides. The three shapes are: blue square represents N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc), green circle represents mannose (Man), and blue circle represents Glucose (Glc). Below this is a large diagram showing the process of oligosaccharide synthesis. This occurs in the lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum. The ER is shown as a large oval for simplicity. It is filled in light purple. The inner purple area represents the lumen. The actual ER itself is represented by a rather thin yellow membrane around the oval, with very thin blue edges to represent the phospholipid bilayer. The initial steps of synthesis (1-3) occur on top of the ER before moving inside it. Step (1) is represented by an arrow pointing left, on top of the ER. On top of the arrow is a convergent-divergent arrow showing addition of 2UDP-GlcNAc and removal of UMP + UDP. Above the middle of the arrow is a circled red X, with a dashed arrow pointing down to it labeled "tunicamycin", indicating that tunicamycin can inhibit this step. The arrow points left to an oligosaccharide structure anchored through the ER and hanging down into the lumen. The structure begins from the bottom with a small orange diamond, connected up to two phosphates (circled Ps) via a short chain. The two phosphates are bonded up to two GlcNAcs. To the left is another arrow pointing left, labeled (2) on the bottom. On top of the arrow is a convergent-divergent arrow showing addition of 5 GDP-Man and removal of 5 GDP. The arrow points left to the oligosaccharide previously described, but with a chain of 5 Man above the GlcNAc. It is on the far left end of the ER, almost to the point where it begins to curve. To the left is an arrow, which curves downward and into the lumen of the ER. It is labeled "(3) Translocation" on the left. The arrow points down to the same oligosaccharide which now has its orange diamond end on the outside of the ER, and the oligosaccharide inside the lumen. It has essentially flipped. Below this oligosaccharide is another arrow, which follows the curve of the ER down and to the right. On the right side of the arrow there are two convergent-divergent arrows. The top one shows addition of 4 dolichol-P-Man (P is circled and represents phosphate) and removal of 4 dolichol-P. The bottom one shows addition of 3 dolichol-P-Glc and removal of 3 dolichol-P. To the right of this arrow is the oligosaccharide, this time with two more Man units attached to the original 5, and three Glc units bonded up to the Man units. To the right of this is another arrow labeled (5). It points right to another structure, which is entering the lumen via an opening in the ER. The structure is a long coiled blue protein with +NH3 bonded to its upper end. The protein is reaching up from an 80S complex (pink rounded top subunit on smaller, rounded purple bottom subunit). The 80S complex has a long mRNA strand beginning left at the 5' end across it; this mRNA reaches continuously across the next three complexes in steps 6 and 7. There is an Asn residue bonded to the left side of the helical blue protein, which has two electrons (red dots) on it. A red arrow represents electron transfer from the Asn to the oligosaccharide. To the right of this image is an arrow labeled (6), pointing right. The arrow points to the next image, which shows the helical blue protein having lengthened and begun to bunch. It still has H3N+ bonded to its end. The oligosaccharide has attached to this blue protein, without the orange diamond and the phosphate groups. The helical blue protein is still attached below to the 80S complex. To the right of this image, still inside the lumen, is another arrow pointing right, labeled (7). The arrow points to the two phosphate groups and the orange diamond, spanning the ER. The phosphate groups are once again back inside the lumen. Above is the helical blue protein attached to the oligosaccharide. The bottom three Man units and the bottom two GlcNAc units have been highlighted beige. To the right of this image is another arrow, which points right before curving up and out of the ER. It is labeled (1). The arrow points up to the 2 phosphate groups, which have again translocated so that they are outside of the membrane with the orange diamond inside. Above this is another large curved arrow, which curves up and left to follow the right end of the ER. It is labeled (9), with a divergent arrow on the right showing removal of Pi. Above this is text reading, "Dolichol phosphate recycled." The arrow continues to curve left until it straightens, pointing left to a single phosphate group outside the ER. It is linked downward to the orange diamond. Below it is dolichol phosphate. To the immediate left of this, the cycle begins anew.
